title: Hybrid Models for Financial Forecasting: Combining Econometric, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models

data_binding.reason: shared benchmark data replaces the paper's native dataset and protocol

requirements: Compute logarithmic returns for the S&P 500 series.
Use an out-of-sample testing/backtest period from 2007-01-01 through 2023-12-31.

dimensions.implication: The benchmark uses a frozen shared dataset rather than the paper's original data.
Only an explicitly named MethodCard model branch may enter the benchmark.

paper_value.preprocessing: Transform price/index data into continuously compounded logarithmic returns. Whether any scaling, normalization, or feature engineering statistics are fit on training data only is unknown.

dimensions.implication: Shared features isolate model behavior but do not reproduce the paper's end-to-end pipeline.

paper_value.evaluation: Walk-forward/rolling evaluation on the S&P 500 out-of-sample period from 2007-01-01 to 2023-12-31. Forecasts are transformed into Long-Short trading signals and evaluated using forecast error metrics and trading performance indicators. Exact signal construction rule and context overlap are unknown.

dimensions.implication: The shared temporal split and metric definitions control comparability across methods.

dimensions.paper_value: transaction costs are mentioned as part of practical trading evaluation, but exact cost values are unknown
dimensions.implication: Trading claims require matched cost and position rules; prediction-only metrics do not establish tradability.

paper_vs_run_delta.original_paper_hypothesis_reason: Shared benchmark data/features/splits differ from the native paper protocol; the original claim cannot be proved or disproved by this run.
paper_vs_run_delta.adapted_task_hypothesis_reason: The method beats the task-appropriate no-leakage baseline.
